TODDLER ROOM LESSON · TODDLER ROOM · AGES 1–3 YEARS

Toy Drum — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches "toy drum" through the copy-cat game: loud, soft, fast, slow — the whole first music curriculum, ending on STOP, hands up, giggle.

What is this?

The toy drum is the red drum with the yellow rims and two sticks — the loudest friend in the room and the first instrument a toddler can truly play.

What does it mean?

Drumming is listening practice disguised as noise: copying a rhythm demands attention. The loud-soft contrast also plants the inside-voice idea in a place where it is FUN.

What does the child need to know?

You need the drum, the sticks and the copy-cat rule: I play, you play. The four contrasts — loud/soft, fast/slow — then STOP, sticks up. The stop is part of the music.

Why this matters

A child who can play loud AND soft owns both volumes. That ownership is the foundation the inside voice gets built on — and the drum is where it is the most fun to practice.

What it teaches

Rhythm copying (attention!), wrist control, dynamic contrast (loud/soft), inhibition on the stop, and the listening half of all music.

Words to learn

toy drumbangloudsoftfastslowstop

Say this to your child

“"Toy drum! Bang bang BANG — loud! Now soft… soft, soft. Copy me — loud! …soft! Fast fast fast… slooow. And… STOP! Sticks up high! Your turn — I’ll copy YOU!"”

Step by step

  1. Introduce the sticks: "toy drum! Bang bang BANG — loud!"
  2. The contrast: "now softly… soft, soft taps." Model with a whisper-face.
  3. Copy-cat: you play loud, they play loud; soft, soft; fast; slow. Four rounds, four contrasts.
  4. The stop: "and… STOP! Sticks up!" Freeze with the sticks in the air — the funniest rule in music.
  5. The encore: their turn to lead, you copy. The teacher seat is the real prize.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "toy drum" sit under a red drum with yellow rims and two crossed sticks — the volume of the room, about to change.

Ask your child

"Bang LOUD!" "Now soft…" "What do we say at the end?" (STOP!) "Your turn — teach me!"

What your child can say or do

Your child might lead the copy-cat game, whisper-tap theatrically, or freeze mid-bang with sticks aloft — dynamics, mastered.

Out in the real world

Loud and soft live everywhere: the vacuum (loud), the cat (soft), the library (whispers). "Drum rules — soft inside!" transfers the whole lesson to daily life.

Try it together

The Volume Song: bang the four contrasts in a fixed order with the song, ending on STOP — the same order daily until the child plays it solo for an audience of teddies.

Understanding check

Ask: "What is this?" (toy drum) "Show me loud… now soft!" "Where do the sticks go at STOP?" (up high!) — bang, contrast, stop: the first concert, complete.

This lesson pairs with the Toy Drum flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Toddler Room.
